Why two quotes for the same New Lenox house come out different

Color matching is the quiet problem on 1997 construction. The original was a builder line that has usually been discontinued, so a partial exterior on one of the 81 percent of New Lenox that is detached houses either gets matched properly or ends up as two shades of the same color on one wall. Worth raising before the work is broken into phases. With 8,334 owner households against 808 renting, New Lenox is about as close to a pure homeowner market as this service area gets. People are painting to keep the house, not to let it, and the scope reflects that.

The lines a quote for New Lenox needs to show

  • Matching, exactly. 10.5 percent of units are attached, and on a shared elevation close is not good enough. Existing color has to be matched rather than approximated.
  • Access, and what it costs. A 1997 median build year means two story walls outside and two story spaces inside. Staging and ladder work belong on the quote as their own line.
  • Finish level. With a median home value of $377,500, the finish standard people expect here is higher than the standard a fast quote is priced at. Worth agreeing before rather than after.
  • Distance, stated. New Lenox is 18.0 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to New Lenox is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
